tagline: Compose, schedule and post to your X account from a local app — with optional rewrites in your own voice via Make It Sound Like Me.
summary: Twitter/X Manager posts to a single X profile through a local Express API using your OAuth 2 user tokens. **Compose** writes and posts a tweet now; the **post queue** schedules tweets for later and a worker in the API posts them when they're due; **Posts** shows history, including your own timeline imported for a date range.

When the integration is enabled, Compose can rewrite a draft so it sounds like you: the API looks up the route in integration-manager's catalog and calls Make It Sound Like Me's create-content integration through the on-device express gateway. History, queue and rewrite ledgers live in local Postgres.
audience: Founders and creators who post to one X account and want scheduling without a SaaS.
You already use Make It Sound Like Me for your voice profile.
You can create an X developer app and generate OAuth 2 user tokens.
notFor: Multiple X accounts or teams — one profile, tokens in env.
Analytics, replies or DMs — compose, schedule, post and import history only.
Running in the cloud — it's a local API with a local secret.

capabilities.title: Compose and post
capabilities.detail: The home page composes a tweet (≤280 chars) and posts it via `POST /api/x/posts`.

capabilities.title: Post queue
capabilities.detail: `/post-queue` schedules text for a time; the API's worker posts due items and records status (`pending`, `posted`, `failed`, `cancelled`).

capabilities.title: Timeline import
capabilities.detail: `POST /api/x/posts/sync` imports your own tweets for a date range (up to 31 days, excluding retweets/replies by default).

capabilities.title: Rewrite in your voice
capabilities.detail: Compose can call MISLM create-content (discovered via integration-manager, executed via the express gateway); each rewrite is logged to `rewrite_text_ai_*`.

capabilities.title: Token refresh
capabilities.detail: OAuth 2 tokens refresh automatically; `X_OAUTH2_PERSIST_TOKENS_TO_ENV=true` writes new ones back to `.env`.

components.name: Web app
components.owns: Compose, post queue and posts screens. Server-side route handlers proxy to Express (`TWITTERX_EXPRESS_URL`) and add `x-local-api-secret`.
components.doesNotOwn: X tokens or the integration key.

components.name: API
components.owns: X API v2 posting and timeline sync with OAuth 2, the post-queue worker, local Postgres `twitterx_manager` (`migrations/`), and the MISLM integration client.
components.doesNotOwn: The rewrite itself — that's Make It Sound Like Me.

dataFlow: The browser calls the web's own `/api/x/*` routes; the web server forwards to Express with `LOCAL_X_POST_API_SECRET`.
Express posts to X API v2 using `CONSUMER_X_ACCESS_TOKEN`, refreshing with `CONSUMER_X_REFRESH_TOKEN` when needed, and stores the result in `x_posted_tweet`.
Queued posts sit in `post_queue`; the worker posts them at `scheduled_at`.

Rewrite: Express fetches the consumer catalog from integration-manager (`INTEGRATION_MANAGER_EXPRESS_URL`), then calls MISLM through the express gateway with `INTEGRATIONS_SERVICES_API_KEY` (and the gate secret when routed via the main gateway).

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: No secrets — not even the local post secret.

trust.title: API (your machine)
trust.detail: X client id/secret and user tokens, `DATABASE_URL`, integration key, optional gate secret.

trust.title: X / MISLM
trust.detail: X receives your posts; MISLM receives drafts you choose to rewrite.

commonTasks.title: First-time setup
steps: Run **Setup** in Hub; create `twitterx_manager` and apply `migrations/` (or **Set up local database** if offered).
In the X Developer Console, create an app with OAuth 2 and generate user access + refresh tokens (scopes incl. `tweet.write`, `tweet.read`, `users.read`, `offline.access`).
Set `TWITTERX_EXPRESS_URL` and the same `LOCAL_X_POST_API_SECRET` on the web, then **Run**.

commonTasks.title: Schedule a week of posts
steps: Open `/post-queue`, add each tweet with its time.
Keep the API running — the worker only posts while it's up.

commonTasks.title: Enable voice rewrites
commonTasks.when: You use Make It Sound Like Me.
steps: Run integration-manager and enable create-content for the `twitterx-manager` consumer.
Set `INTEGRATION_MANAGER_EXPRESS_URL` and `INTEGRATIONS_SERVICES_API_KEY` (same as MISLM's), plus `ON_DEVICE_DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET` if routed via the main gateway.

commonTasks.title: Import past tweets
commonTasks.when: You want full history in Posts.
steps: Run a sync for a date range (≤31 days per call); repeat for older ranges.

troubleshooting.fix: The access token expired and refresh failed, or the app lacks `tweet.write`. Regenerate tokens; consider `X_OAUTH2_PERSIST_TOKENS_TO_ENV=true`.
The API wasn't running at the scheduled time, or the post failed — check its status and error on `/post-queue`.
integration-manager isn't running on `INTEGRATION_MANAGER_EXPRESS_URL`, the consumer isn't enabled, or the integrations key doesn't match MISLM's.

glossary.definition: Scheduled tweets posted by the API's worker.
Catalog service that tells consumers which integration routes are enabled.
MISLM's integration endpoint that rewrites text in your voice.
Scope for history rows until real auth exists (default `default`).

hubNotes: Port clashes: this API's 3081 is also the default storage port in estimate-and-proposals' and finances-manager's `.env.example`, and the web's 3082 is estimate-and-proposals' API default.
The registry has no `localDatabase` entry, so create `twitterx_manager` and apply `migrations/` by hand.
Voice rewrites depend on `~/github/integration-manager` (port 3099) and make-it-sound-like-me, neither started by this project.
API README is still the template; the web README and ADRs are current.
